model.rationale: Goldman holds a heavily Republican Fort Worth-area seat, has a large financial advantage and outside support, while the Democratic challenger shows no fundraising footprint and no polls exist. Prediction markets price the race around 95% Republican, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin near R+15.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger competitive, or a major scandal or late outside spending against Goldman, would be the main reason to move the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-12 is a solidly Republican Fort Worth-area district with an 11-point Republican lean. Incumbent Craig Goldman, first elected in 2024, is running for reelection and has raised about $1.76 million with $1.5 million on hand, plus modest outside support. Democratic challenger Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has no reported fundraising or cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Goldman's win probability around 95 percent. The expected margin is roughly 15 points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
